title: Thermal history of ~1 TeV pseudo-Dirac dark matter with the LZ-fitted coupling: freeze-out, coannihilation and non-thermal production
question: Is the coupling giving one LZ event at delta = 250-390 keV consistent with thermal freeze-out (coannihilating chi1/chi2, mediator pairs), non-thermal production (moduli decay, freeze-in, asymmetric DM) or the gauge-fixed Higgsino relic, for m = 0.3-10 TeV in the Higgsino, dark-photon and heavy-Z' families, and what non-thermal fraction, dilution D or T_RH is needed where thermal production fails?
headline_result: delta ~ 300 keV changes freeze-out by <= 2e-10 (first-order Griest-Seckel effect cancels); freeze-in (overproduction 1e25-1e33) and asymmetric DM (oscillation in 1/delta = 2e-21 s) are excluded; a thermal relic fits one LZ event only for a 1025-1290 GeV Higgsino at delta = 360-385 keV, a secluded dark photon at delta <= 356 keV (1 TeV; any delta with D = 1.3-2.3), or a contact Z' at delta <= 298/318 keV (B-L/U(1)_B, 1 TeV); contact Z' models need T_RH < 5 MeV beyond delta = 372/377 keV and are excluded there
model_or_mechanism: pseudo-Dirac DM (Higgsino; kinetically mixed dark photon; heavy B-L / U(1)_B Z'); Boltzmann freeze-out with g*(T), Griest-Seckel coannihilation, contact-limit fixed point, annihilation-limited non-thermal production, entropy dilution, UV freeze-in, chi-chibar oscillation
result_type: computed (relic solver, fixed points, windows); estimated (T_RH, Planck floor, eps ceiling)
confidence: medium - solver validated to 3% and P054 reproduced, but Sommerfeld, halo and recalled bounds shift delta-boundaries by ~10 keV
